FlickAtlas review

Overall: 5/10.

  • Action & Cinematography: 5.5/10
  • Comedy & Entertainment: 5/10
  • Direction: 5/10
  • Music & BGM: 6/10
  • Performances: 6.5/10

Story & Plot

In Masterplan, a legendary thief named Roger Cavendish sets his sights on stealing the Mona Lisa by recruiting two young strangers, only to reveal they are his long-lost children and he is their father. The newly reunited family is thrown into a chaotic heist, utilizing a criminal underworld version of Tinder to enlist help from Italian tech whiz Chiara. Along the way, the crew engages in plenty of thievery, manipulation, and twists as they attempt to pull off the caper.

Comedy & Entertainment

The film attempts to channel the spirit of late-20th-century crime comedies and caper films with a tart, slightly farcical and lightly sardonic tone. Reviewers note that the movie knows it is ridiculous, which aids its watchability even if the writing struggles to fully land its comedic and emotional aspirations. It relies on standard genre machinery and a Guy Ritchie-esque mood board to drive its entertainment value.

Performances & Direction

Stanley Tucci leads the cast as the felonious Roger Cavendish, bringing his established range to the caper alongside Simona Tabasco, who plays Italian tech whiz Chiara. The ensemble cast also features Victor Belmondo, Eliott Margueron, and Barbara Lo Gaglio. While the screenplay squanders some of its emotional potential, the actors do what they can with the material provided.

Strengths

  • Stanley Tucci leading the cast
  • A colorful world conjured by director Thomas Vincent
  • A stylish musical mood reminiscent of Bond and Shaft
  • An intriguing initial heist premise involving the Mona Lisa

Weaknesses

Despite a promising setup, the screenplay fails at every level by squandering its emotional throughline and leaving the estranged-sibling and father dynamics feeling half-assed. The writing offers an unconvincing veneer of sentimentality over routine plot machinery, hampered further by a torrent of harsh language and content issues.

Final verdict

Masterplan leans heavily on familiar caper tropes and a high-concept premise involving the Mona Lisa, but ultimately falters under the weight of a weak screenplay. While Stanley Tucci's presence and a colorful visual style offer some watchability, the overall execution feels empty. It is a strictly skippable streaming option for viewers seeking a truly sharp crime comedy.

Story & Plot

Set against the vibrant backdrop of a 1960s-inspired, retro-futuristic multiverse world, Marvel's First Family must balance their roles as heroes with their strong family bonds. The narrative follows married scientists Reed Richards and Sue Storm, alongside Johnny Storm and Ben Grimm, as they work together to protect Earth. They are forced to defend their home from evil extraterrestrial forces, including a ravenous space god called Galactus and his enigmatic Herald, Silver Surfer.

Comedy & Entertainment

The film delivers a briskly paced and entertaining superhero adventure that rattles along with a refreshing clarity of purpose. Reviewers note that it is fun, enjoyable, and smart without being cold, maintaining an engaging atmosphere throughout the brisk runtime.

The cast features strong performances from Pedro Pascal as Reed Richards, Vanessa Kirby as Sue Storm, Joseph Quinn as Johnny Storm, Ebon Moss-Bachrach as Ben Grimm, and Ralph Ineson. While the movie is largely enjoyable, reviewers note that it is a flawed production with a familiar setup that tosses viewers straight into the deep end from the first frame. Some viewers may find the heavy reliance on multiverse lore and comic book-style action to be a standard formula.

The Fantastic Four: First Steps serves as a solid foundation and a successful course correction for the team. With strong performances and a vibrant retro-futuristic world, it comes recommended as a fun adventure for fans of the genre.
